judged_text: `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` silently no-ops when destinationCalendar is null (the case when neither eventType nor organizerUser has one), and the preceding teamMemberPromises loop reads `user.destinationCalendar` from user objects whose select (dynamic-user prisma select / eventType.users) is not shown to include the destinationCalendar relation. For collective events where the organizer has no destination calendar, all team members' destination calendars are silently dropped instead of being used, so no per-host calendar events are created; if the user query select lacks destinationCalendar the push list is empty for every collective booking regardless.

adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, `evt.destinationCalendar` is explicitly set to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists (`destinationCalendar: ... : null`). Immediately after, for collective team events, the code does `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);`, which will not push anything when `destinationCalendar` is `null` (optional-chaining no-op). This drops the collected `teamDestinationCalendars` and can prevent per-host destination calendars from being applied. The second claim (that `user.destinationCalendar` isn’t selected in the user query) is not fully verifiable from the diff because `userSelect.select` / host selection is not shown, but the null + optional-chaining drop is directly evidenced in the diff.
